correctness.rationale: For distinct rank-one constants A→a and B→b, two nonempty equal composites would force A=B and a=b. Thus commutation is exactly mutual zero products, b not in A and a not in B. For image set H and complement R, each image can carry one map whose domain contains that image, or a nonempty selection from the 2^|R|−1 nonempty domains contained in R; choices at distinct images are independent. This gives P_n. A maximal clique must saturate any external image, which then uses every point of R in its domains and prevents any new image. If there are no external images, the only extension risk is an unused point of R; its singleton identity can be added exactly when that point is absent from every domain. Each point in R must therefore assign itself to a nonempty subset of the self-domains. These two disjoint cases prove M_n, including R empty. For h<n the size is at most h(2^(n−h)−1), strictly below 2^(n−1)−1 if h>=2 by h<=2^(h−1). The h=n case has size n. At n>=4 this leaves exactly n one-image cliques of all external maps. The proof's one-image equality sentence at RESULT.md line 43 should be restricted to n>=3 (and h<n): at n=2 a singleton self-map ties the external size one, but the maximum is two and the finding does not claim its maximizer classification there. Independently reconstructed direct pointwise compositions and counted all cliques and extensions for n=1–4, confirming every coefficient, with P_4 total 1376, M_4 total 221, and four degree-7 terms counted with multiplicity. Small-case checks do not replace the uniform argument.

evidence: The trivial-group 0-Rees representation uses a row for every nonempty domain, a column for every image, and a nonzero sandwich entry iff the domain contains the image. There is no nonzero central vertex for n>=2: for a given constant choose a different domain containing its image and the products do not commute.

Theorem 5.4 gives the extremal size from maximal zero submatrix area (and small diagonal cases). For h selected image columns the largest zero submatrix uses 2^(n−h)−1 rows, so the maximum is 2^(n−1)−1, with the n=2 diagonal exception and n=3 tie. At n>=4 a maximum clique has size >n and must repeat an image. The transposed repeated-index argument in Case 4 bounds its size by h(2^(n−h)−1), forcing h=1 and all compatible domains. Thus that extremal information is already implied.
The full partial-transformation graph includes higher ranks; its clique number does not give the restricted polynomials.

value.rationale: Rank one is a canonical stratum of the partial transformation monoid. The two labelled polynomials give fine information not determined by its already covered clique number: how idempotent and external-domain choices combine, and when every possible extension is blocked. The exact distinction between ambient and induced maximality is useful in comparing partial maps with relations and partial bijections. The coverage of extremal size alone does not reduce the two enumerators to a rephrasing.
